content.text: The text satirizes corrupt civic leaders, exploitative employers, religious hypocrisy, and workers’ resignation to poverty. The Town Council approves dubious contracts, inflated salaries, and schemes benefiting its members, while Dr Weakling alone objects. Rushton and Misery drive painters and builders through intimidation, unsafe conditions, wage insecurity, theft, and deliberate shoddy work. Workers remain divided, suspicious, and hostile to Socialism, though Owen and Barrington advocate public ownership, organized production, leisure, education, and shared prosperity. Their ideas provoke violent opposition at socialist meetings near Windley’s Cross Roads. At the “Refuge,” Philpot chairs Barrington’s lecture on Socialism, held in a makeshift pulpit during heavy rain. The workers’ Beano travels by brakes to the Queen Elizabeth at Tubberton, where they eat, drink, sing, argue, and celebrate their employer despite exploitation.
